outcome: Phase of labor at hospital admission (latent vs. active)
cohort: 375 low-risk women (150 in group prenatal care and 225 in standard prenatal care) with certified nurse-midwives (CNMs)
finding: Women who received group prenatal care were more likely to be in active labor and had greater cervical dilatation at hospital admission compared to those who received standard prenatal care.
mod_finding: This study did not examine mode of delivery but found that women receiving group prenatal care were more likely to be in active labor upon hospital admission compared to those receiving standard prenatal care.
